Hey all,

My name is Michael and I recently migrated back over to the Windows world after nearly 8 years with Macs. I grew up with XP so this transition wasn't too hard, and when I picked up my Surface Pro 3 I finally understood Windows 8 - it's an operating system for the Surface that works fantastic and was clunky as hell for any normal PC.

My worries about Windows 10 is that I'm going to lose a lot of what I love about Windows 8 on my surface, so I'm actually in the middle of upgrading to the Windows 10 preview right now. I wanted to pop over here (since I'll be using Voat instead of Reddit moving forward) to see if anyone here had any requests or questions about Win10, the SP3, or both in concert.

Just let me know if there's anything you'd like me to test, and I'm looking forward to getting to know you all!

EDIT1: Whoops, forgot to include which SP3 I have. It's the i7, 8 gig, 128 internal HDD model. I just finished the upgrade, and it is choppy as all get to start out with. I went through the website to upgrade, and it kept everything in place as it was in my 8.1 installation. If my performance doesn't increase after some tweaking and a reboot, I might just try to do a full wipe and reinstallation (still trying to figure out if that's possible at this point).

EDIT2: I'm just gonna talk to the wall for now. Definitely not working out well at all with a very noticeable and jarring lag to every action. Since it was an upgrade and not a full installation (I always prefer the latter over the former), I'm going to wipe the drive and install a clean copy of Windows 10. Should take an hour or so and I'll update afterwards if there is any improvement.

EDIT3: Huh, didn't see that coming. Turns out the full reset option inside of Windows 10 restored me back to a vanilla 8.1 Pro install. No worries - starting the upgrade again, this time with a fresh computer.

EDIT4: In case anyone finds this later, this restore and upgrade is taking forever. Forgot I'd have to run the firmware upgrade again before the Win10 preview could be installed. Finally back to upgrading now, based on the last upgrade it should be done within the next hour or so. Only problem is I found a blog (https://www.thurrott.com/windows/windows-10/3142/windows-10-technical-preview-2-surface-3)) that recommended I change the upgrade path and run any outstanding updates which might tack on another hour or so

EDIT5: Final edit for a while. Finally got up to build 10130 and ran all of the updates available. Initial impression is very impressive at this point. After some starting sluggishness, which I suspect might have been due to indexing, the OS is incredibly fluid. The ability to jump between tablet and PC mode is incredibly well done, the OS runs very smooth on my SP3, and I actually kind of like this new browser (which was born from the ashes of it which must not be named). All in all, very good start for a developer release.

I'll be checking in on this post so if you stumble across this and have any questions / requests please don't hesitate to respond!

Final Fantasy VII - E3 2015 Trailer | PS4

This is exciting news, but I'm honestly surprised Square-Enix will even attempt this. FF7 has been promoted to a legendary status among it's fans, and I am not sure if any level of quality will ever be good enough for them. But then again, Black Mesa did a great job with Half-Life, so it is possible to do.

It will not live up to the hype. There is nothing that they can do that will satisfy the millions of fans who have proclaimed this one of the best games of all time.

If they do nothing but make an HD port asshats will complain that it was just a port and didn't change anything about the gameplay. If they do make changes to the gameplay asshats will complain that they changed the game too much.

What Square is really doing is writing a license to print money. VII is going to make a killing no matter how well it is received. It will review well and most certainly be one of the best selling games the year it is released. The can then go back and make VI, VIII and IX and take in the nostalgia money.

People want those games back. X was the first of the terrible FF games. XII and XIV are hot garbage.VII, VIII and IX are the golden era and people will pay through the nose for them

Personally X is my favorite and I loved XII. I think XIII is the biggest pile Square Enix ever shoveled out.

What's interesting about the FF series is that each fan has a completely different opinion from the next. They tried to make their games unique from each other, and in turn now have multiple audiences they need to cater to who want different things.

Just out of curiosity, how old are you? I only ask because I've noticed almost the same thing myself. I'm 33. One of the first games I ever played on my NES was Final Fantasy. I have a super nostalgic love for that game and FFIV. I consider VI the highmark for storytelling in the series and I've already stated my opinion on the PS1 versions.

X was the departure of the open world system and went on rails. However, most of my little brothers friends, about 6-8 years my junior fucking love that game.

I'm 25, so right in that age difference you mention. There is an on-rails feel, but since the goal is clear from the very beginning, it doesn't feel forced to me. The game still rewards exploration, but keeps you on track. Later in the game you get the airship and can revisit anywhere in the world.

I think probably my favorite part is the characters in FFX.

  • Wakka is, hands down, the best bro of any game I've ever played. His character is as real as it gets, and his arc throughout the game makes him truly shine.
  • Auron, the spirit of vengeance tied to the mortal realm until he can redeem the deaths of his best friends.
  • Tidus, the manifestation of a celebrity of a long-dead city. He was their sports hero in life, and becomes a true hero in after life.

The only characters I can think of that are as interesting to me are Cloud and Sephiroth from FF7. I don't remember much about FF8 or FF9, as they didn't appeal much to me story wise.

Yeah, there has to be something in those 8 years that sets people apart. Wakka and Tidus are two of my most disliked characters of all time.

Either way, bring on the remakes. As long as they're released eventually on the Xboner, I'll buy em.
I couldn't stand Tidus, and the laughing scene with Yuna. My god, the JRPG was strong in that one.

If I'm correct, FFX was the first game that let you do more than 9999 damage and that was the most memorable of the game. I did enjoy Blitzball, but the margin of error was very high so much so that if you really wanted a nearly unbeatable roster you had to quit the game and load it if you lost one match.

Oh when FFXIII-2 came out and I saw the opening scene I was really excited about it. Seeing Lightning with her Valkyrie armor and fighting in that cinematic opening really hyped it up. Then, it was nothing like that.... it was just horrible.

My favorite thing that people say about 13 is..."Just play through the first 48 hours or so then the game will really open up." You know what FF13 fans? I did i played all the way until the game opens up and it still stinks.

I actually did enjoy it once you made it to the final stretch and could free roam and manage your party, and honestly if it had been that way after the first 3 hours or so the game would have been much better.

But the story and characters were still beyond redemption. I don't want to play through an entire game where all the characters are crying and trying to commit suicide.

If they do nothing but make an HD port asshats will complain that it was just a port and didn't change anything about the gameplay. If they do make changes to the gameplay asshats will complain that they changed the game too much.

Under no circumstances should they change anything but the art style and assets. Changing core gameplay would be far an away the biggest blunder their company has ever made.

Not just saying this ironically to meet your criteria for angered fan, I'm saying this is supposed to be an HD remake, that's all. That's how it should stay. Changing an award winning gameplay formula, which is the primary reason people want it remade, would be disastrous.
I have a little hope that they could do it well. But with what they have been releasing in the last couple of years... I don't want to put too much faith in them.

Ok. So I'm one of those people. FF7 is my favorite game of all time. Sure, yes, FF6 and Chrono Trigger come really damn close, but FF7 is special.

I can't put it into words, I can't explain exactly why. It was the right game, at the right time. I fell in love with that game. I taught myself to play most of the music on piano. I ravenously searched for the secret that would bring her back after disc 1. I still get emotional listening to the music. The Materia system is still the best spell system FF ever came up with.

I hated all the spin off material. None of it felt right, like it was just thrown together to carry the name, the spirit was gone.

All that said... I'm going to get behind this. I think I will like it no matter what. I miss my friends. I miss hanging out in the gold saucer, I miss skimming the clouds in the Highwind, I Cid, Vincent, RedXIII, yes even Yuffy.

Lately I've been feeling a little too close to this and I think seeing them again, as themselves, in a new light will be good, no matter how bad it is.

It's a cut above 9/10 remakes that come out these days. I remember where if you wanted to do a remake, you had to do what the Resident Evil Remake for Gamecube or Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes did. Actually REMAKE the game. Only recent game that's done this was Black Mesa. Now we get shit like The Last of Us: Remastered, Journey on Ps4, Metal Gear Solid HD Collection, ICO & Shadow of the Colossus on Ps3. Not that these games are bad. In fact, the games I just listen are all probably in my top ten favorite games list. But the way they were remade was just sad. At least this is a cut above the rest. That being said, I would rather Square-Enix just make a GOOD FF game.

We were actually discussing what might be new, the same guy that was going to be screaming about the news actually. We had a good discussion about the length of the game and if anything would be cut out. The FF games now are not that lengthy compared to old games, understandably because of better graphics, but it would be a shame if they cut out any part of the original game just to save on time and graphics. The battle system is going to be something that should be taken very seriously, as I wouldn't want the game to be turned based anymore, and I wouldn't want stupid gimmicks like FF's PSP game, god I forgot what the name was but the system used random numbers for special attacks that you had no control over.
